title: Runbook-driven deployment coordinator with traffic-tilt validator and autorevert advisor
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Motivation: production teams repeatedly ask for a guided, auditable handoff between automated rollout automation and operator-driven runbooks when a deployment sees noisy signals. This PR introduces a Runbook-driven Deployment Coordinator that bridges automated promotion logic with human-run runbooks and a new safety surface called the traffic-tilt validator. The coordinator also ships an Autorevert Advisor that scores the confidence of an automated revert and provides actionable remediation steps and cost/SLO impact estimations.

What this changes (high level):
- New coordinator service (deploy/coordinator) that orchestrates staged validations, optionally pauses for runbook checkpoints, and emits deterministic checkpoints to the ledger for replay.
- Traffic-tilt validator: lightweight online tester that checks small, time-windowed traffic perturbations (tilts) across latency, token-error, and soft-quality measures to detect regressions that only appear under low-volume perturbations.
- Autorevert Advisor: inference that aggregates metric delta, anomaly score, and estimated cost delta to recommend either auto-revert, partial rollback (slice-only), or human escalation.
- Console UI additions: a runbook checkpoint timeline and an inspector for the traffic-tilt samples.
- Telemetry and alerts: new metrics (deploy.runbook.checkpoint, deploy.tilt.sample_rate, deploy.autorevert.score) and dashboards.
- Runbook manifest schema (YAML) and example runbook with smoke steps and rollback playbook.

Checklist: - [x] Coordinator runtime + API surface implemented - [x] Traffic-tilt validator integrated into the coordinator flow - [x] Autorevert Advisor scoring + test harness - [x] Console wiring + basic e2e smoke - [x] Documentation (docs/deploy/runbook.md) - [x] Integration tests for tilted samples and advisor decision gating

Backwards compatibility: existing deployment manifests remain valid; the coordinator is opt-in via a new field deploy.policy.runbook.enabled=false/true. If disabled, behavior is unchanged. Autorevert Advisor runs in dry-mode by default and must be enabled via org policy to perform automatic reverts.

Testing notes: unit tests cover coordinator state machine transitions, tilt sample reservoir behavior, and advisor decision boundaries. Integration tests exercise a staged deployment with synthetic latency and quality regressions. Load-tested coordinator under simulated parallel rollouts (10 concurrent).

Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature-flag; enable in staging for 2 weeks with telemetry collection; flip advisor to dry-run in production for small cohorts; enable auto-revert for internal orgs after confidence window.

Related: links to the runbook schema and example in the docs: docs/deploy/runbook.md, Linear ENG-4321 for product acceptance criteria, Support ticket SUP-1122 for an incident that motivated the tilt approach.

review_thread: Ethan Jacobs: Nice separation of concerns. A few questions on coordinator guarantees: what happens if the ledger write fails during a checkpoint?

Priya Kapoor: If ledger write fails we mark the checkpoint as PENDING and schedule exponential backoff; the coordinator will not advance a cutover until the checkpoint is confirmed. Added retry logic in ledger_client.py (see commit a9f3b2c).
Marta López: Tilt sampling looks promising. Can we ensure the reservoir doesn't bias towards long-running requests? Consider weighting by request age.
Priya Kapoor: Good point — the reservoir uses an age-decayed weight; added a unit test to cover that behavior (test_tilt_reservoir).
Kenji Sato: Autorevert Advisor thresholds feel conservative. For orgs that want faster rollback, can we expose the scoring weights via org policy?
Priya Kapoor: Yes, advisor weights are configurable via deploy.policy.autorevert.weights and documented in docs/deploy/runbook.md. Kept safe defaults for orgs that opt-in to auto-revert.
Ethan Jacobs: CI flaked on the first run (integration timeout). Re-ran and green. Approving after addressing ledger retry and adding a comment in docs about operational cost implications.
Marta López: UX nit: the tilt inspector should display raw sample histograms alongside the score. I added a follow-up TODO in the console file.
release_notes: Add Runbook-driven Deployment Coordinator, Traffic-Tilt validator, and Autorevert Advisor. Opt-in via deploy.policy.runbook.enabled. New metrics: deploy.runbook.checkpoint, deploy.tilt.sample_rate, deploy.autorevert.score. See docs/deploy/runbook.md for examples and runbook manifest schema.
